title: Motor Electronics Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: The motor electronics coolant temperature sensor circuit is out of range.
fullDescription: P0A00 concerns the inverter / motor electronics cooling loop. Hybrids and EVs use a dedicated low-temperature loop for the inverter, motor, and on-board charger. Loss of cooling will quickly trigger thermal derate and shutdown.
safetyImpact: Inverter overheating leads to power-train derate or shutdown; do not drive aggressively.
symptoms: Check Engine Light or service-vehicle warning
Reduced power / EV power limit warning
Coolant pump audible noise or silence

fixSteps.title: Inspect Coolant Level
fixSteps.instruction: Check the inverter (low-temp) coolant reservoir, not the engine reservoir.

fixSteps.title: Bleed Air from Loop
fixSteps.instruction: Run the manufacturer's bleed routine via the scan tool to purge air.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Compare temperature sensor resistance to spec at known temperatures.

fixSteps.title: Replace Pump or Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install replacement and re-bleed system.

faq.q: Can I drive in this state?
faq.a: Briefly, at light load. Continued operation will derate or disable the hybrid system.

faq.q: Is hybrid coolant the same as engine coolant?
faq.a: It is the same chemistry but in a separate, lower-temperature loop with its own reservoir.

title: Engine Failed To Start
shortDescription: Engine Failed To Start fault detected by the hybrid powertrain control module.
fullDescription: P0A0F is set when the hybrid PCM identifies an unexpected condition in the high-voltage drive system. These faults usually trigger a 'Service Hybrid System' indicator and frequently disable EV mode until repaired.
safetyImpact: Hybrid system may be disabled; reduced power and possible no-start.

causes.cause: Failed component identified by code description
HV battery state of health degraded

fixSteps.title: Scan All Modules
fixSteps.instruction: Use a hybrid-capable scan tool to retrieve codes from every controller.

fixSteps.title: Inspect HV Connectors
fixSteps.instruction: After confirming the HV system is de-energized per the service manual, inspect connectors for corrosion or arc damage.

fixSteps.title: Module Software Update
fixSteps.instruction: Check the manufacturer for applicable reflashes.

fixSteps.title: Replace Identified Component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the failed module or sensor following OEM HV safety procedure.

faq.q: Can a non-hybrid shop fix this?
faq.a: Most shops are not equipped or trained for HV service; use an EV/hybrid specialist.

faq.q: Is the high-voltage system dangerous?
faq.a: Yes. HV systems can deliver lethal current; never service without proper training and equipment.

fixSteps.instruction: Use a hybrid-capable scan tool to retrieve codes from every controller.

fixSteps.title: Inspect HV Connectors
fixSteps.instruction: After confirming the HV system is de-energized per the service manual, inspect connectors for corrosion or arc damage.

fixSteps.title: Module Software Update
fixSteps.instruction: Check the manufacturer for applicable reflashes.

fixSteps.title: Replace Identified Component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the failed module or sensor following OEM HV safety procedure.

faq.q: Can a non-hybrid shop fix this?
faq.a: Most shops are not equipped or trained for HV service; use an EV/hybrid specialist.

faq.q: Is the high-voltage system dangerous?
faq.a: Yes. HV systems can deliver lethal current; never service without proper training and equipment.

title: High Voltage System Interlock Circuit
shortDescription: HV interlock loop fault detected.
fullDescription: P0AA0 concerns the high-voltage battery cooling subsystem. Most hybrids cool the HV pack with cabin air pulled through a filter, while EVs use liquid cooling. Blocked filters, failed blowers, or refrigerant loop faults trigger this family of codes.
safetyImpact: HV battery overheating accelerates capacity loss and can trigger total power-train shutdown.

causes.cause: Clogged HV battery cabin air filter
Failed HV battery cooling fan or pump
Sensor failure within the HV pack

symptoms: Audible HV cooling fan running constantly

fixSteps.title: Inspect HV Battery Air Filter
fixSteps.instruction: Locate the HV battery cabin filter (often behind the rear seat) and replace if dusty.

fixSteps.title: Test HV Cooling Fan
fixSteps.instruction: Command the HV cooling fan with a scan tool and verify operation.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Refrigerant Loop
fixSteps.instruction: On liquid-cooled packs, check refrigerant pressure and chiller bypass valve.

fixSteps.title: Pack-Level Diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: If sensor or capacity faults persist, plan for OEM-level pack diagnostics.

faq.q: Will replacing the cabin filter clear P0AC0?
faq.a: It often will if the only cause was airflow restriction; verify with a follow-up drive cycle.

faq.q: How long do HV battery packs last?
faq.a: Most modern packs last 8-15 years; deterioration codes appear when capacity drops well below new.
